A single car\\u0027s sticker does not prove a trim lacks an optional feature, so the Corolla LE\\u0027s push-button start stays unknown in the can record a window-sticker equipment reading for one VIN by hand, so a sticker read outside the walk (a PDF, a photo) settles that car\\u0027s keyless-entry, smart-key, and push-button-start status.\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022A command such as \\u0027odo equipment set \\u003Cvin\\u003E --push-button-start absent|present --smart-key-entry ... --keyless-fob-entry ... --source \\u0022\\u003Ctext\\u003E\\u0022\\u0027 stores each given status on the vehicle with source \\u0027sticker (manual)\\u0027 plus the given text, under the same precedence as a walked sticker (sticker over trim table).\u0022,\u0022A later walked sticker or a later manual entry replaces it; odo show prints the source; rank applies it, so a manual \\u0027absent\\u0027 for a required feature excludes the car with that reason, the same as a walked sticker.\u0022,\u0022Tests cover setting, overriding, and the rank exclusion; docs/commands.md documents the command.\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Feature\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022From the 2026-10-03 shortlist session: shortlist #105 JTDBCMFE0S3083487 (2025 Corolla Hybrid LE) has a Toyota sticker PDF (notes/stickers-2026-10-03/ in the project home) showing no push-button start, but odo reads stickers only from walked detail pages and never from PDFs, so it reads unknown. Brian\\u0027s rule is to exclude a car only when its sticker confirms a feature missing; this gives that rule a way to see a sticker read by hand. No network
